stories.headline: Nvidia books TSMC's 1.6nm A16 for Feynman GPUs, skipping 2nm entirely

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is reported to have booked TSMC A16 capacity for Feynman, its post-Rubin GPU architecture, with mass production set for the second half of 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is reported to have booked TSMC A16 capacity for Feynman, its post-Rubin architecture GPU. ... A16 is scheduled for production readiness in H2 2026 and mass production of Feynman is set for H2 2028.

key_facts.fact: A16 is TSMC's 1.6nm successor to its N2 2nm node, using gate-all-around transistors and backside power delivery, and delivering 8-10% more density and speed than N2P with 15-20% less power.
key_facts.excerpt: A16 is TSMC's 1.6nm successor to its 2nm process N2 with GAA transistors and backside power delivery. It delivers 8-10% more density and speed than N2P with 15-20% less power.

key_facts.fact: Feynman would be Nvidia's first architecture to use TSMC's SoIC 3D chiplet stacking, backside power delivery, custom HBM and co-packaged optics; the current Rubin and Rubin Ultra generations are built on TSMC's N3 3nm process.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA plans its next-gen Feynman GPUs for H2 2028 using TSMC's A16 1.6nm process instead of N2/2nm, introducing 3D chiplets via TSMC SoIC, backside power delivery, next-gen packaging, custom HBM, and co-packaged optics

key_facts.fact: TSMC's COUPE photonic packaging would give Feynman over 1,000TB/s of total system bandwidth, against 520Tb/s for Rubin.
key_facts.excerpt: Using TSMC's COUPE (Compact Universal Photonic Engine) technology gives Feynman over 1,000TB/s total system bandwidth compared to Rubin's 520Tb/s.

key_facts.fact: The report, sourced to DigiTimes, says TSMC is accelerating its AP7/AP8 packaging capacity toward a potential 50,000-wafer ramp by the end of 2027; neither TSMC nor Nvidia has confirmed the claims.
key_facts.excerpt: Although TSMC and NVIDIA haven't confirmed or responded to the report's claims, it suggests TSMC is aiming to hit 50,000 wafers by the end of 2027 to pave the way for Feynman's arrival in the second half of 2028.

sources.title: Nvidia books TSMC 1.6nm process for Feynman in H2 2028

stories.headline: Google reportedly taps AMD for a CPU-heavy TPU v10, AMD's first custom AI ASIC

key_facts.fact: A SemiAnalysis client note says market chatter puts Google and AMD on a TPU project in the v10 generation, which would be AMD's first real involvement in a custom AI ASIC project.
key_facts.excerpt: "Market chatter suggests [Google] is working with AMD on a TPU project in the v10 generation," a SemiAnalysis note for clients cited by Sean reads. "AMD's involvement would be the first real involvement in a custom AI ASIC project, despite having a custom silicon team."

key_facts.fact: The stated draw is AMD's IP in advanced packaging and SoIC plus its CPU cores, because Google and its customers are pushing for TPUs with on-package CPU cores for reinforcement-learning workloads.
key_facts.excerpt: "AMD has strong IP, especially in advanced packaging and SoIC. Additionally, CPU IP could also be a draw given Google and its customers are pushing for TPUs with on-package CPU cores for RL workloads."

key_facts.fact: Google has already been adding general-purpose compute around its accelerators: TPU 8i inference systems pair one Google Axion CPU with every two TPUs, versus one Intel Xeon 'Emerald Rapids' per four TPUs in seventh-generation systems, and a 1:1 ratio is reportedly optimal in some cases.
key_facts.excerpt: Its TPU 8i systems, designed for inference, reasoning, and RL workloads, feature one Google Axion CPU for every two TPUs. By contrast, servers running Google's 7th Generation TPUs used one Xeon 'Emerald Rapid' processor for every four TPUs. Furthermore, we are hearing that in some cases a 1:1 ratio of CPUs to accelerators is optimal

key_facts.fact: Google has designed nine generations of TPUs with Broadcom acting as the silicon designer, so analysts see low odds of AMD implementing the v10i inference or v10t training chips outright.
key_facts.excerpt: Google has designed nine generations of TPUs with Broadcom acting as silicon designer, so it hardly needs AMD for a conventional accelerator. SemiAnalysis argues the chances of AMD implementing the v10i inference or v10t training chips are low

key_facts.fact: AMD's precedent is the Instinct MI300A, which integrates 24 Zen 4 x86 cores, 228 CDNA 3 compute units and 128GB of unified HBM3 with 5.3TB/s of peak bandwidth in one package.
key_facts.excerpt: With the MI300A, AMD has integrated 24 Zen 4 x86 CPU cores, 228 CDNA 3 GPU compute units, and 128GB of unified HBM3 into a single package. Peak memory bandwidth reaches 5.3TB/s.

key_facts.fact: Nothing is confirmed: neither Google nor AMD has commented, and 'TPU v10' is not a product name Google has announced — Google's publicly announced eighth generation is TPU 8t and TPU 8i, unveiled at Google Cloud Next in April 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: neither Google nor AMD has announced a TPU v10 or any joint design effort. ... "TPU v10" itself is not a product name Google has announced; it is a term used by SemiAnalysis. ... What Google has officially announced are its eighth-generation TPUs, TPU 8t and TPU 8i, announced at Google Cloud Next in April 2026

stories.headline: Meta and BlackRock's $14B El Paso data center is insured for under $500M, FT finds

key_facts.fact: The Financial Times reported that Meta and BlackRock's $14bn El Paso data centre leaves lenders exposed to an insurance gap, with investors in gigawatt-scale campuses facing billions in underinsured risk as insurers balk at the cost of full coverage.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta and BlackRock's $14bn data centre exposes lenders to insurance gap — Investors in gigawatt-scale campuses face billions in underinsured risks as insurers balk at cost of full coverage

key_facts.fact: The Sopaipilla project carries insurance limits of $427 million during construction and $450 million once operational, against roughly $14 billion in total development costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta and BlackRock's $1 billion Texas Sopaipilla data centre has insurance limits of $427 million during construction and $450 million operational, leaving potential coverage gaps.

key_facts.fact: S&P rated the Sopaipilla debt A-plus, citing bondholders' lack of claim on the assets and Meta's ability to terminate the lease after 18 months of delays.
key_facts.excerpt: S&P rated the Sopaipilla debt A-plus, citing bondholders' lack of claim on assets and Meta's ability to terminate the lease after 18 months of delays

key_facts.fact: The El Paso campus is a 1-gigawatt AI site so large that conventional insurance markets can only cover part of it; broker Marsh handled the project risk analysis and observers describe a 'data center insurance supercycle'.
key_facts.excerpt: A 1-gigawatt AI campus in El Paso is testing the limits of what the insurance industry can price and cover. ... Risk advisory firm Marsh is involved in the project's risk analysis, and industry observers describe the current moment as a "data center insurance supercycle"

key_facts.fact: Because lenders and institutional investors require insurance as a financing condition, partial coverage adds friction to deal structuring and can raise the cost of debt on every $10bn-plus campus.
key_facts.excerpt: Lenders and institutional investors require insurance coverage as a condition of financing. When coverage is partial or non-standard, it creates friction in deal structuring and can raise the cost of debt.

stories.headline: FT: 60 planned US data centers would emit 101.5M tons of CO2 a year, 7% of the power sector

key_facts.fact: A Financial Times analysis of the 60 largest data centers Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Meta plan to build in the US found they could emit 101.5 million tonnes of CO2 a year once operational under the current US generation mix.
key_facts.excerpt: An analysis by the Financial Times of 60 large data centers that Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Meta plan to build in the United States found that the facilities, once operational, could emit 101.5 million tons of carbon dioxide a year, the newspaper reported on the 16th local time.

key_facts.fact: That is about 7% of total US power sector emissions last year, equivalent to the output of 27 coal-fired plants or 24 million gasoline cars.
key_facts.excerpt: That figure is about 7% of total U.S. power sector emissions last year and equals the output of 27 coal-fired power plants or 24 million gasoline-powered cars.

key_facts.fact: Three-quarters of the utilities supplying the 60 sites are planning or building new gas-fired capacity, 17% told regulators they are building new gas plants specifically for hyperscale data centers, and a third of those with coal plants are delaying closures.
key_facts.excerpt: three-quarters of the utilities supplying power to the 60 data centers are planning or building new gas-fired generation capacity. Seventeen percent of the utilities told regulators they were building new gas-fired plants to meet the power demand of specific hyperscale data centers. One-third of the utilities that operate coal-fired plants are also delaying plant closures.

key_facts.fact: The companies' own reports already show emissions rising: Amazon up 16% from 2024 to 2025 (with purchased-electricity emissions up 34%), Microsoft up 25%, and Alphabet's ambition-based emissions up 18%.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon says its emissions rose 16 per cent from 2024 to 2025, with data-centre construction and delivery fuel among the drivers, while electricity-purchase emissions increased 34 per cent. Microsoft says its total emissions rose 25 per cent over the same period, primarily because of expanding data-centre infrastructure, and Alphabet says its ambition-based emissions increased 18 per cent

key_facts.fact: Energy researcher Jonathan Koomey called the estimate a reasonable ballpark and a significant increase on what data-center operators said five years ago they aimed to achieve under their emissions-reduction plans.
key_facts.excerpt: Jonathan Koomey, an energy researcher focused on efficiency and climate solutions, says the figure is a reasonable ballpark estimate and marks a significant increase from what data-centre operators had said they aimed to achieve five years ago under their emissions-reduction plans.

stories.headline: WSJ: nine tech firms carry ~$3T in off-balance-sheet AI commitments, five times reported capex

key_facts.fact: An analysis of securities filings found nine tech companies had roughly $3 trillion of off-balance-sheet commitments, mostly AI-related — about triple what they owe under their outstanding leases and long-term borrowings.
key_facts.excerpt: 9 tech cos had~$3T of off-balance-sheet commitments, mostly AI-related, an analysis of securities filings shows, about triple what the companies owe under their outstanding leases and long-term borrowings. Eye-opening report by @rudegeair and @pswsj

key_facts.fact: The commitments — massive spending pledges for data-center leases and chips — are not shown on the companies' balance sheets, and far exceed the roughly $600 billion in capital expenditure they report.
key_facts.excerpt: nine top tech companies including Alphabet and Meta had ~$3T of AI-related off-balance-sheet commitments, far exceeding their $600B in reported capex. Massive spending commitments for data-center leases and chips aren't shown on companies' balance sheets

key_facts.fact: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft alone now account for more than $2.4 trillion of those future off-balance-sheet commitments.
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft now have more than $2.4 trillion in future off-balance-sheet commitments - WSJ

key_facts.fact: The commitments are described as mainly leases that have not yet commenced plus contractual pledges to buy capacity, energy, servers, cloud services or infrastructure — locking in a large share of future compute demand.
key_facts.excerpt: Not hidden debt but mainly leases that have not yet commenced and contractual commitments to purchase capacity, energy, servers, cloud services or infrastructure. ... A significant portion of future compute demand is therefore already locked in.

stories.headline: Japan's largest AI data center planned for Akita at ¥2 trillion, with UAE fund circling

key_facts.fact: A project is underway to build one of Japan's largest AI data centers in Akita Prefecture, aiming to start operations as early as 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Akita, Aug. 17 (Jiji Press)--A project is underway to build one of Japan's largest artificial intelligence data centers in the northeastern prefecture of Akita, aiming to launch operations as early as 2030.

key_facts.fact: The project is led by S2, a server management firm based in the city of Akita, and US startup Bitgrit, with total construction costs estimated at about ¥2 trillion ($12.5 billion).
key_facts.excerpt: The plan is being led by S2, a server management firm based in the city of Akita, and U.S. startup Bitgrit, with the total construction cost estimated at ¥2 trillion ($12.5 billion).

key_facts.fact: Total power-receiving capacity is slated to reach up to 500 megawatts, and further investment of several trillion yen could follow depending on demand and expansion.
key_facts.excerpt: The data center's total power-receiving capacity is slated to reach up to 500 megawatts, making it one of the largest in Japan. Additional investment amounting to several trillion yen could be made depending on future demand and facility expansion.

key_facts.fact: S2 and Bitgrit plan to set up a special purpose company to raise investment and financing from domestic and overseas institutions; a United Arab Emirates sovereign wealth fund has shown interest.
key_facts.excerpt: S2 and Bitgrit plan to establish a special purpose company to seek investments and financing from domestic and overseas financial institutions and investment funds. A sovereign wealth fund from the United Arab Emirates has shown interest in investing in the project, according to the companies.

key_facts.fact: The site would sit in an industrial zone to be developed by the city and prefecture in northern Akita, which the companies hope will attract AI businesses and workers to the region.
key_facts.excerpt: The firms are cooperating with Akita Prefecture and the city of Akita with an aim to make the data center a hub to attract AI-related businesses and human resources.

sources.title: Akita eyes AI data center that could become Japan's largest
One of Japan's Largest AI Data Centers to Be Built in Akita

stories.headline: Chipmakers backed $250B of startup rounds in 2026, with Nvidia in a record 59 deals

key_facts.fact: The semiconductor sector's most valuable companies have so far in 2026 participated in startup rounds collectively valued at over $250 billion, multiples above prior high marks, per Crunchbase data.
key_facts.excerpt: So far this year, the sector's most valuable companies have participated in rounds collectively valued at over $250 billion, per Crunchbase data. That's multiples above prior high marks.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's record $122 billion March round — in which Nvidia was one of eight lead investors — accounts for over 95% of the value of all semiconductor-company-led financings this year.
key_facts.excerpt: This includes OpenAI's record-breaking $122 billion March funding round, in which Nvidia was one of eight lead investors. ... That one deal accounts for over 95% of the value of all semiconductor company-led financings.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has participated in a record 59 known funding rounds so far this year, up from 53 in all of 2025, and has led or co-led at least 11; its market cap is around $5.4 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: The AI chip architect has participated in a record 59 known funding rounds so far this year, per Crunchbase data, up from 53 in all of 2025. With a market cap around $5.4 trillion ... having led or co-led at least 11 private company financings this year

key_facts.fact: AMD has backed 19 private financings this year, at least four of them valued at $1 billion or more, while Samsung has made at least 17 known startup investments.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD, with 19 private company financings this year, is also upping its startup investment activity ... This year's tally includes at least four rounds valued at $1 billion or more. Another standout is Samsung, with at least 17 known startup investments so far this year.

key_facts.fact: Chip companies have invested in more than 60 startup financings of $100 million or more in 2026, 16 of them valued at $1 billion or above; one was Nvidia's $5 billion July financing for Safe Superintelligence.
key_facts.excerpt: So far this year, corporate semiconductor giants have invested in more than 60 startup financings of $100 million or more. Of those, 16 rounds were valued at $1 billion or more ... Take July's $5 billion corporate financing from Nvidia for foundational AI startup Safe Superintelligence.
